A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MADE benchmark. All 22 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, are readable. Retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original computational discovery experiments across intermetallic systems, including policy comparisons, system-size and stability-threshold analyses, and discovery-diversity results in Table 1 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds generator comparisons, agent ablations, alternative LLM evaluations and results on additional chemical families in Tables 4–6.

M1.justification: The MADE rollout, benchmark classes, diversity-planner equations and default LLM orchestration procedure remain unchanged. Additional generators, LLMs and component-removal configurations are evaluated within the existing framework; they do not introduce a redesigned proposed method.

E1.justification: v2 retains the 30 intermetallic systems and adds 10 systems each from chalcogenides, halides and oxides, explicitly listed in Table 3 and evaluated in Appendix C.6/Table 6. This substantially broadens the chemical domains actually tested.

E2.justification: Tables 4–5 expand the evaluated comparison sets beyond Random/Chemeleon generators and GPT-5.1. OMatG is tested with Random, Diversity and LLM planners; MatterGen is tested with random selection. Additional orchestrators use Claude Sonnet 4.6, DeepSeek v3.2 and GPT-5.4 Nano.

E3.justification: Appendix B.4.7 revises reported filter application from all policies to the LLM orchestrator and MLIP-ranking policies; this does not establish that experiments were rerun. New ablations vary reasoning limits and history length, while MatterGen uses chemical-system conditioning. The underlying 50-query budget, five episodes per system, oracle and metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's pipeline-component, system-size and stability-threshold analyses, Appendices C.4–C.5 add generator and LLM comparisons and ablations of MLIP tools, generator tools, structural information, reasoning steps and history length. These substantially expand investigation of which components support agent performance.

E5.justification: Both versions report five independent episodes per system and standard errors of the mean. The added tables follow the existing uncertainty-reporting practice. No new repeated-run scheme, confidence-interval procedure or significance-testing method is documented.

E6.justification: Tables 4–6 add substantial generator, agent-ablation, LLM and chemical-family results. For example, Table 5 reports AUDC 0.48(2) without the MLIP tool versus 0.40(2) for the default agent. Figure 7 also changes the illustrated acquisition outcomes. Table 1's numerical differences are equivalent rounding, not demonstrated performance changes.

T1.justification: The discovery-policy definition, stability condition, optimization objective, metric formulas and diversity-planner equations are retained. No new theorem, proof, derivation or substantive mathematical revision appears.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a modular closed-loop discovery benchmark and evidence that adaptive planning becomes more important as search difficulty increases. v2 emphasizes this finding in the abstract, but v1 already states it in the introduction and conclusion. The additional experiments support the existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning misleading surrogate scores, direct LLM structure proposals, reasoning depth, memory, structural context and transfer across chemical families. It also recommends matching component-training data to the reference set and warns of recall from larger generator training sets. Some new interpretations overreach: Table 5 shows mixed structural-context and reasoning-depth effects, while Table 6 contains planning policies below the random baseline.

D1.justification: Appendix C.4 adds implementation and checkpoint references for MatterGen and OMatG, including MatterGen's chemical_system checkpoint and guidance factor 2. Table 5 documents the added model and control configurations. Existing hardware, prompts, relaxation settings and code-access information remain; GPT-5.1 and StructureMatcher details were already disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds Höllmer et al. for OMatG and replaces the cited Settles 2011 work with the 2012 Active Learning book. The related-work arguments and Appendix A positioning remain essentially unchanged. Abhyankar's retitled conference publication corresponds to the previously cited preprint.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Section 4 to Section 2, with corresponding renumbering. The abstract is tightened, experimental cross-references are expanded, and affiliation, publication and acknowledgment text changes. Most existing prose and appendix explanations are retained, so this is a limited reorganization rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial comparison displays in Tables 4–6 and expands Table 3 into grouped chemistry-family columns. Figure 7 is redrawn with larger labels and a shared legend. The original Figures 1 and 2 exchange numbering and placement, and several other displays move while retaining their content.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's narrow empirical demonstration of benchmark generality by adding three chemical families, alternative generators and LLMs, and agent-component ablations. Tables 4–6 make dependence on chemistry, models and tools directly inspectable, while checkpoint details and the recall caveat improve transparency. Some new interpretations overstate the evidence, particularly reasoning-depth benefits and consistent planning gains, but these weaknesses do not outweigh the substantial expansion of evidence supporting and qualifying the benchmark.
